thought.text: Clean environment. Now let me start the Docker build. I'll run it in the background to avoid the 600s command timeout.

reasoning_content:
Clean environment. Let's start the docker environment with `docker compose up -d`. This will build images, might take a while. Set USER_ID/GROUP_ID? The guide doesn't mention it, compose has defaults. Let me export USER_ID=1000 GROUP_ID=1000 maybe. Actually defaults in Dockerfile are 1001 if not set, but compose passes empty string as arg. In the Dockerfile ARG USER_ID then ENV USER_ID=$USER_ID then ENV USER_ID=${USER_ID:-1001}. But since ARG USER_ID is set to empty string "" (not unset), does ${USER_ID:-1001} use 1001? The `:-` operator uses default when unset OR null (empty). So empty gives 1001. Fine. But addgroup --gid "" ... actually ${GROUP_ID} in RUN expands to... ARG was ""? Hmm if ARG is empty, `${GROUP_ID}` in RUN expands to empty → addgroup --gid  ${GROUP_NAME} would error. Wait but ENV GROUP_ID=${GROUP_ID:-1001} sets it to 1001. The RUN commands use the ENV value (1001) since ENV overrides. Actually ARG and ENV same name: ENV takes precedence in subsequent RUN. ENV GROUP_ID=${GROUP_ID:-1001} — at that point GROUP_ID refers to the ARG (empty) → 1001. Then ENV set to 1001. So fine.

Let's just build. This will take significant time (composer install, npm ci during build for web). Let me run docker compose up -d with a long timeout. The tool timeout is 600s fixed. Builds may exceed. Let me do docker compose build first maybe. Actually `docker compose up -d` builds and starts. 600s may not be enough for building 3 images (web builds Next.js). Let me build each separately.

Let me start with docker compose build --parallel maybe. Actually let's just do it and observe. I'll set USER_ID/GROUP_ID to 1000.

Better: run builds in background with nohup and poll. But the terminal command has 600s timeout, killing the shell? If I use nohup and redirect, the build continues. Let's do that.

Actually, simpler: run `docker compose build` and see how far within 600s. Docker layer caching persists between commands. Let me run it.

Let me first pull base images maybe. Just go.

I'll run build with nohup in background to avoid timeout issues.

action.command:
cd /workspace && export USER_ID=1000 GROUP_ID=1000 && nohup docker compose build > /tmp/build.log 2>&1 &
echo "started pid $!"; sleep 20; tail -5 /tmp/build.log
